name: Cinder
blurb: A moth that collects the dust of fallen stars.

chapters.title: The First Flutter
chapters.text: Cinder arrived on a breath of warm air, folding her dusty wings like a small grey book. She had flown a long way, she said, following the smell of blooming moonlight. "Gardens grow toward whatever glows," she whispered, settling on a leaf. "And you have made something very bright here." She stayed until the petals stopped swaying, then slept with her wings open, catching every star-spirit that drifted past.

chapters.title: Dust of Faraway Stars
chapters.text: Cinder showed you the dust on her wings. Each speck, she explained, was a crumb of a falling star, gathered from ten thousand quiet rooftops. "Stars shed a little when they fall," she said. "It is how they say goodbye." She brushed her wingtip over the moonpetals, and where the dust landed, tiny sparkles woke and floated up like slow, delighted bubbles.

chapters.title: A Place to Rest
chapters.text: Cinder had decided your garden was her favorite rest stop between the sky and the ground. "Most places are too loud," she murmured, curling her antennae into two sleepy spirals. "But here, the flowers hum instead of shouting." She tucked herself under a wide glow bloom, and if you looked closely, you could see the star dust rising and falling with her breathing, like the tiniest constellation learning to sleep.

name: Luna
blurb: The garden's oldest guardian, permanently mid-yawn.

chapters.title: The Yawning Guardian
chapters.text: Luna glided down without a sound, which is the way owls say hello politely. She was mid-yawn, a great soft yawn that lasted almost a minute, and when she finished she blinked at the garden with warm amber eyes. "I guard this wood," she said, "from nightmares. But your garden is so calm that I mostly just guard its naps." She folded her wings like a blanket and stayed until the moon moved.

chapters.title: What Owls Know
chapters.text: "Every goodnight has a sound," Luna told you, perched on the tallest star tree. "Rain says hush. Wind says soon. And gardens," she added, ear feathers tilting, "say come back tomorrow." She let you listen to the leaves for a while. Underneath the quiet there was a slow rhythm, like the garden breathing, and Luna nodded as if to say: that is the sound. That is the one.

chapters.title: Keeping Watch, Softly
chapters.text: Luna stayed a whole evening this time, half-dozing with her beak tucked in, one eye occasionally drifting open to check on the moonpetals. "Nothing needs me tonight," she reported, sounding pleased about it. "That is the best kind of watch." Before she flew home, she pressed her forehead gently to the tallest bloom, and for the rest of the night that flower glowed a little warmer than all the others.

name: Pip
blurb: Carries a tiny lantern-heart that lights up when he snuffles.

chapters.title: Snuffling In
chapters.text: Pip did not arrive so much as appear, nose-first, from behind a fern. He snuffled the air once, twice, then waddled into the open as if he had always lived here. His small heart-lantern glowed warm through his spines. "I follow cozy smells," he explained. "Trailing starlight. Warm soil. Kind hearts. You have all three." He curled up between two moonpetals, and his lantern dimmed to a sleepy ember.

chapters.title: The Spine Library
chapters.text: Pip's spines, it turns out, are a library. Each one holds a feeling he wants to keep. "This one," he said, carefully showing a pale spine, "is the night I first heard a lullaby. This one is warm rain." He let you touch one, very gently, and a soft green glow traveled down it like a note being read. "Gardens are where I file the best ones," he said.

chapters.title: A Debt of Warmth
chapters.text: Pip arrived carrying a leaf bundle, which he nudged toward the biggest bloom. Inside was a pile of tiny glowing berries. "A thank-you gift," he said shyly. "For the nights I have slept here." He buried most of them around the roots "for the flowers' dreams," ate two, and then curled into a ball beside you, lantern-heart ticking softly like a pocket watch counting pleasant thoughts instead of seconds.

name: Selene
blurb: Hops down moonbeams and carries a drop of night in her paws.

chapters.title: Down the Moonbeam
chapters.text: Selene came the way moonlight comes through a curtain: suddenly, softly, everywhere at once. One moment the glade was empty; the next, a pale rabbit was sitting in it, holding a single glowing dewdrop in her paws like something precious. "I collect the night's last drop," she said. "It is always found in the calmest garden." She looked around slowly. "This one qualifies." She placed the drop in your pond, where it rang like a tiny bell.

chapters.title: The Slow Hop Home
chapters.text: Selene showed you her secret path home: a moonbeam, walked slowly. "Rabbits rush," she said, "but moonbeams do not allow it. Every hop must land inside the quiet." She practiced while you watched, hopping in slow motion up a shaft of silver light, ears floating behind her like two soft exclamation marks. At the top she paused, waved one paw, and the beam faded like a sigh.

chapters.title: Dream Banking
chapters.text: "I run a small bank," Selene confided. "For dreams. You deposit a good one, and later, exactly when you need it, it comes back with a little extra." She tapped the ground with her paw three times, and a circle of moonpetals glowed faintly in reply. "Your garden has a healthy balance," she concluded. "Many calm nights deposited. And tonight," she said, curling up with her ears over her eyes, "another one."

name: Glimmer
blurb: Never in a hurry, always exactly on time.

chapters.title: The Slow Arrival
chapters.text: You first noticed Glimmer by his light: a small golden glow traveling up the garden path at the speed of patience. He was a snail with a lantern shell, and he left a trail of glittering night-dew behind him. "Hello," he said, in a voice like a small door opening. "I am not late. I am early for tomorrow." He admired each flower for a long, unhurried while, and his shell lit up brightest beside the oldest ones.

chapters.title: What the Trail Remembers
chapters.text: "My trail remembers everything," Glimmer said. He pointed with one eyestalk at the faint silver line behind him. "This part is the smell of your star trees. This bend is where a moth laughed. Gardens go by so fast for everyone else," he sighed happily, "but my trail keeps them." He drew a slow loop around a dewbell, closing it like a sentence. "There. Now tonight is kept forever, exactly this cozy."

chapters.title: Lantern Lessons
chapters.text: Glimmer stayed up all night teaching his lantern to shine in your garden's favorite color. It took hours. Snail lanterns, he explained, can only change one shade per evening, and only while the snail is perfectly content. "Almost," he murmured, watching the glow shift from gold to soft green, then to a green like sleeping leaves. "There." He smiled in the way snails do, which is entirely with the light. "Now I can carry a piece of your garden with me."

name: Ember
blurb: Curled like a campfire, warm as one too.

chapters.title: A Warm Shape in the Dark
chapters.text: Ember arrived as a warm patch of dark-and-amber, curled at the edge of the glade like a small sleeping campfire. His tail was wrapped around his nose; only one ear tracked you as you passed. "I nap where the air feels kind," he murmured, without opening his eyes. "Your garden has the right kind of hush. The kind that lets a fox keep one ear on the stars and the rest of himself on sleep."

chapters.title: The Tail of Nine Sparks
chapters.text: Ember's tail, he explained between yawns, stores nine sparks — one for each truly peaceful night he has ever slept. "They are not for burning," he said, lifting his tail so you could see the tiny lights riding in the fur. "They are for remembering." He showed you the newest spark, still bright. "That one is from here. From the night the moonpetals hummed and a hedgehog snored in B flat."

chapters.title: Night Watch Exchange
chapters.text: "Every garden needs a fox on the soft hours," Ember declared, taking up a dignified post beside the tallest star tree. His duties, as he described them, included: greeting shooting stars, approving the color of the moon, and growling politely at any worry that wandered too close. At dawn he stood, stretched each paw in turn, and touched his nose to your hand. "Watch kept," he reported. "All peaceful. You may sleep extremely well."

name: Droplet
blurb: Sings the sound the rain will make tomorrow.

chapters.title: The First Note
chapters.text: Droplet announced herself with one small, perfect note — a sound like a raindrop deciding to be music. She sat on a lily pad of light in the middle of the pond, throat glowing gently. "I sing tomorrow's rain," she said. "It is a preview. Very exclusive." She sang three more notes: a soft one, a rounder one, and one that wobbled like a jellyfish riding a bicycle. Somewhere far away, clouds began to smile.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for the Sky
chapters.text: Droplet held a full rehearsal that night. "The sky must never be surprised by weather," she explained, tuning her throat-glow with one thoughtful toe. She sang the whole piece: beginning drizzle, middle shimmer, and a finale of big fat gentle drops that she performed simply by blinking in rhythm. The pond carried every note outward in slow silver rings. "Perfect," she said at last. "Tomorrow's rain will sound exactly like being tucked in."

chapters.title: The Pond Remembers
chapters.text: Droplet taught you the pond's oldest song, the one it sings to itself when no one is listening. "Frogs only share it with gardens that glow," she said. The song was simple: three notes up, one long note down, and then a rest — and in the rest, if you held very still, you could hear every lullaby the pond had ever learned, all humming together under the water like sleeping bells.

name: Astra
blurb: Purrs in constellations; tail tip is a small star.

chapters.title: The Silent Pounce
chapters.text: Astra arrived the way cats arrive at the best parties: already there, sitting on something important. In this case, the moon. No — on a moonpetal, which is nearly the same thing. Her tail ended in a small steady star. "I heard a purr-worthy garden from three skies away," she said. She patted a drifting mote of light, pounced gently on it, and let it go. "Yes. This one will do nicely."

chapters.title: Purring in Constellations
chapters.text: "Cats purr in constellations," Astra told you, arranging herself into a perfect loaf. "Every purr is a tiny sky." She let you listen: deep and slow, the purr wrapped around the garden like a blanket, and the fireflies began drifting into the shapes her purr described — a ladle, a lyre, a fox chasing a very slow rabbit. "That one is my favorite," she said, watching the firefly-rabbit. "It never gets caught. It just naps mid-hop."

chapters.title: The Nine-Nap Treaty
chapters.text: Astra formally proposed a treaty between your garden and all star cats: nine naps, in nine chosen spots, forever renewing. She inspected each proposed nap spot personally — behind the glow bloom, under the star tree, the warm flat stone — and approved all of them by lying on each one for exactly as long as a nap requires. "Treaty sealed," she declared at moonset, tail-star blinking slowly. "You may pet the treaty. Once. Softly."

name: Flicker
blurb: A spark that learned to be curious.

chapters.title: A Very Small Visitor
chapters.text: Flicker was the smallest visitor the garden had ever had, a bright bead of light with two leaf-thin wings and enormous curiosity. She inspected everything: the dew, the petals, the sleeping frog. "What is that?" she asked about eleven hundred times. "And that? And that?" When she finally ran out of questions, she sat down on a moonpetal, sighing a tiny golden sigh. "Gardens," she concluded, "are the best kind of almost-magic."

chapters.title: The Lantern Trade
chapters.text: Flicker proposed a trade: one spark of her lantern-light for one glow of your garden's brightest bloom. "Fair trades make friendships glow longer," she said solemnly, which is old sprite wisdom. The exchange took four seconds and one soft chime, and afterwards her spark burned with a hint of moonpetal-violet, and your bloom glimmered with a hint of mischief. "Good trade," she said. "We are now officially part of each other's light."

chapters.title: Learning to Be Bright
chapters.text: "Being bright is a skill," Flicker said, hovering upside down. "Most sparks flash. The clever ones breathe." She demonstrated: brightening on the inhale, softening on the exhale, until she pulsed in time with the garden itself — with the sway of the blooms, with the frog's slow blink, with your own breathing, if you let it. "There," she whispered proudly. "Now you know the deepest sprite secret. Brightness is just gentleness, done on purpose."

name: Velvet
blurb: Antlers that catch falling starlight like a trellis catches vines.

chapters.title: Steps in the Deep Grass
chapters.text: Velvet walked in slowly, each hoof landing like a comma in a very kind sentence. Starlight had gathered in her antlers the way dew gathers on spider silk, so she seemed to carry a small chandelier of sleeping stars. "I heard the garden from the far woods," she said. "Gardens that glow are worth the walk." She lowered her head and let one star from her antlers roll off onto a moonpetal, where it settled in comfortably.

chapters.title: The Night Orchard
chapters.text: "There is an orchard beyond the last hill," Velvet told you, "where the trees grow sleepy fruit." She described it while grazing politely at the garden's edge: pears that taste like the quiet after a yawn, plums that taste of blanket corners. "But the trees only wake for tired travelers," she said. "Which is everyone, eventually." She left a single glowing fruit beneath your star tree, just in case tonight was that night.

chapters.title: Antler Constellations
chapters.text: Velvet stood very still under the sky while the starlight in her antlers rearranged itself into tiny constellations — a deer, a gate, a garden gate open just a crack. "They are maps," she explained softly. "Every kind place I have ever slept leaves a star behind." She tilted her head so you could see the newest one, bright at the base of the left antler. "That is yours. It will be in my map forever now."

name: Nimbus
blurb: Drifts at garden altitude, sings to the flowers in whale-light.

chapters.title: The Drift overhead
chapters.text: The garden grew suddenly soft, and you looked up into the kind eyes of Nimbus, a whale the size of a friendly weather system, floating just above the tallest star tree. "I patrol the night skies for restless gardens," he rumpled, in a voice like distant, happy thunder. He sprayed a thin arc of stardust from his blowhole, and it fell over the flowers as the gentlest possible rain. "All calm here," he noted. "Carry on."

chapters.title: Whale-Light Lullabies
chapters.text: Nimbus sang that night — long, low notes that moved through the garden like warm currents through deep water. "Whale-light songs travel at the speed of sleepiness," he explained afterward, glowing faintly blue along his belly. "By the second verse, flowers are dreaming. By the third, stones." The whole garden swayed slightly, even the pond, and when the song ended every moonpetal held a tiny note of blue light that faded only at sunrise.

chapters.title: A Whale's Promise
chapters.text: Before drifting on, Nimbus made you a promise, pressing his vast soft brow against the sky above your garden. "When you cannot sleep," he rumpled, "look up. Somewhere above your roof, I will be swimming the slow lane, keeping the night smooth for you." He rolled once, entirely, which is how whales wave goodbye, and then dissolved upward into the stars, leaving a trail of warm cloud that smelled faintly of lullabies.

name: Sage
blurb: Older than the garden's oldest seed; walks at the speed of wisdom.

chapters.title: The Slowest Hello
chapters.text: It took Sage the whole evening to cross the garden, and he considered every step worth it. His shell was a dome of deep green scattered with points of ancient light — constellations so old they had retired. "I visit gardens that have finished becoming gentle," he said, in a voice like a book opening. "Yours qualifies." He settled beside the tallest bloom and began a blink that would last, by his estimate, until the moon moved twice.

chapters.title: Shell Stories
chapters.text: "Every tortoise shell is a library," Sage said, and invited you to look. The constellations on his back rearranged slowly as he spoke: a seed, a sprout, a garden, a friend. "That last one is new," he noted. "It is shaped like you, standing here." The stars held still so you could see. "Shells remember what gardens feel like," he said. "So that even in winter, somewhere it is still soft, and still glowing, and still waiting."

chapters.title: The Garden's Grandmother's Grandmother
chapters.text: Sage knew the very first moonpetal, he said. It grew where the first lullaby was ever sung, and every moonpetal since has been trying to sing it back. "Your garden is close," he told you, nodding slowly — so slowly the nod lasted a full minute. "Listen." You both listened. Under the leaves, under the pond, under the stars, there it was: the oldest lullaby, humming up through the roots, patient as a tortoise, and just as sure of arriving.
